title: kv-cache: improve memory eviction, defrag & spillover heuristics (v38)
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and aggressive spillover under mixed workload profiles have been a recurring source of latency variance and increased GPU memory pressure. This PR refactors the eviction pipeline and tuning heuristics to reduce fragmentation, improve paging efficiency, and favor low-latency paths for hot prefixes. High level changes: 1) Introduces a two-tier eviction policy (age+weight) that prefers evicting sparse/fragmented entries while preserving dense hot spans; 2) Adds an adaptive spillover threshold that is workload-aware (sequence-length distribution + live allocation pressure) to avoid premature GPU->CPU paging; 3) Implements an incremental defragmentation pass driven by the defrag_coordinator that runs opportunistically during low-util windows; 4) Exposes runtime knobs for defrag aggressiveness and spillover bias via flags and config; 5) Adds instrumentation and new metrics (kv.defrag.* and kv.spillover.*) and end-to-end benchmarks. Description of changes: - runtime/kv_cache/eviction.rs: rewrote eviction selection to compute a fragmentation score per entry and a combined cost metric = age_score * weight_factor + frag_score * frag_factor. The default frag_factor is small but increases under memory pressure. - runtime/kv_cache/spillover.rs: adaptive threshold logic that samples request seq length histogram and active allocations to tune the spillover threshold. Adds hysteresis to prevent thrashing. - runtime/kv_cache/defrag_coordinator.rs: new coordinator that schedules lightweight compaction passes on partially-free memory segments. Coordination uses existing scheduling hooks to avoid interfering with critical inference batches. - runtime/scheduler/policy.rs: updated policy to prefer placements that reduce fragmentation by co-locating temporally adjacent KV ranges when feasible. - bench/perf/kv_cache_bench.cc and bench/perf/configs/latency-heavy.toml: benchmark harness updates and new workloads used in CI. - docs/kv_cache.md: docs describing new flags, metrics, and recommended tuning recipes. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior; flags are opt-in for more aggressive defrag. Testing: unit tests for eviction scoring and spillover thresholding; integration tests in perf harness compare baseline and new policy. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-3245) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration perf tests - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated - [x] Migration guide in docs Performance results (summary): In our internal perf lab on A100-40GB with mixed chat+completion workload (50% short sequences <64, 50% long sequences up to 2048) we observe: - 18% reduction in 95th percentile token latency for cold-hot mixed workloads - 12% reduction in GPU memory variance (stddev of usage across runs) - 22% fewer spillover events under peak allocation compared to v37 (measured over 1M requests) Rollout plan: Initially enable on dedicated perf and canary pools for 72h with automatic rollback if kv.spillover.rate increases >10% or kv.defrag.failed_passes >5. If safe, promote to Dedicated and Hosted regions on a staged cadence. Related: references pr-412999, pr-441500, pr-371234 for earlier heuristics.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) core: eviction heuristics v2 and frag score computation; 2) coordinator: incremental defrag coordinator + scheduling hooks; 3) perf/docs: benchmarks and docs updates
benchmark_results: A100-40GB mixed workload: p95 token latency -18% vs v37; GPU memory variance -12%; spillover events -22% over 1M requests. Bench harness config and raw logs attached to the PR artifacts.
release_notes: Improved KV cache eviction and defragmentation heuristics to reduce fragmentation and spillover. Adds new runtime knobs and metrics: kv.defrag.* and kv.spillover.*. Opt-in aggressive defrag mode available via config.
review_comments: Diego Morales (2026-02-22): Left a couple of questions on frag_score weight tuning — can we expose the frag_factor as a dynamic config?
Ava Chen (2026-02-22): Reply: frag_factor is already exposed as a runtime knob; added docs and default conservative value. Added test coverage for dynamic updates.
Priya Nair (2026-02-24): Observed a 2% regression in tail latency on the extremely-short workload. Can we gate the defrag on a util threshold?
Ava Chen (2026-02-24): Added util-based gating so defrag is skipped for >95% short-seq traffic. Re-ran bench and included results in PR description.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-26): Approved after CI run and bench artifacts looked good. Recommended a 72h canary rollout plan which is included in the PR.
